draft.title: Reactivity of metals
card: Reactivity is how readily a metal reacts with other substances, such as water, acids and oxygen. A more reactive metal reacts faster and more vigorously.
Reactivity is found by experiment. Students compare what they see, such as how fast bubbles form or how quickly a metal tarnishes, under the same conditions.
Ranking metals from most reactive to least reactive gives a reactivity series. In it, potassium, sodium and calcium are high, magnesium and zinc are in the middle, and copper and gold are low.

A metal high in the series reacts strongly with acid. A metal low in the series reacts weakly or not at all. For example, magnesium fizzes quickly in dilute hydrochloric acid, but copper shows no reaction.
draft.remember: The faster and more vigorously a metal reacts, the higher it sits in the reactivity series.

a.q: Pieces of zinc, magnesium and copper of equal size are placed in dilute acid. Magnesium fizzes fastest, zinc fizzes slowly and copper does not react. What does this show?
opts: Magnesium is more reactive than zinc, and zinc than copper
Copper is more reactive than zinc, and zinc than magnesium
Zinc is the most reactive, as it reacts at a steady pace
All three have the same reactivity, but differ in size
a.why: The faster the reaction, the more reactive the metal, so the order is magnesium, then zinc, then copper. Copper showing no reaction does not make it the most reactive. It places it lowest in the series.
a.clue: Faster, more vigorous reaction means higher in the series.

b.q: Priya tests four metals in dilute acid. Metal W produces no bubbles, X produces a few slow bubbles, Y produces rapid bubbles, and Z produces bubbles at a medium rate. Which list orders them from most reactive to least reactive?
b.why: Rapid bubbles mean the most reactive metal (Y), then medium (Z), then slow (X), then no reaction (W). The list W, X, Z, Y reverses the order by treating no reaction as most reactive.
b.clue: Rank by how fast bubbles form, fastest first.

a.best: Magnesium is more reactive than zinc, and zinc than copper
